results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We head back to Constantionple with Jonathan Greig at the controls, to discuss the quintessentially Orthodox mystic, Maximus the Confessor. Late-Platonist apophasis meets hard-core ascesis, and Maximus follows the theology where it wants to go, sometimes to his own cost.

results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We pick up from our last episode, where geopolitics and esotericism met in the crucible of Roman, Sassanian, and Arab political struggles. Ahab Bdaiwi threads the labyrinth of the earliest historical sources for the birth of the movement within Islām which came to be known as the Party of ‘Alī, or the Shi‘ā.

results.trackName: Seventh-Century History for Students of Western Esotericism
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We return to the history of late antiquity in the eastern Mediterranean and central Asia. Momentous events occur, empires rise and fall, and Jews, Christians, and Muslims all suddenly develop new apocalyptic notions. Come for the dry historical exposition, stay for the esoteric divine kingship.

results.shortDescription: We use the history of the text of the Qur'ān, from oral revelation to written ‘book’, as both a cool story and as an opportunity for various reflections on more esoteric aspects of the text.
results.trackName: Introducing the Qur’an Part III: Qur’ānic Texts vs. the Qur’ān
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss some of the history of how the Qur'ān came to be ‘the Book’: it started in the oral milieu of the high-octane early Believers' movement, and ended up in written form as something called the ‘Uthmanic recension. Many esoteric things happen along the way.

results.trackName: Introducing the Qur’ān, Part II:  Ambiguity and Esoteric Themes
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We begin to explore the esoteric side of the Qur'ān, examining several case-studies in terms of ambiguity and esoteric themes. It turns out that every letter of the Qur'ān is an esoteric text.

results.trackName: Introducing the Qur’ān, Part I: Revelation, Text, and History
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We cover some basic territory in introducing the Qur'ān, the holiest text of Islām. We introduce the text, discuss the traditional story of the Qur'ān's revelation, the modern text-critical enterprise of Qur'anic studies, and try to pin down the elusive character of this book-that-is-not-a-book.

results.trackName: Fred Donner on the History of Early Islām
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss what little we know and how much we don't know about the nature of the early ‘Believers' movement’, the nature and origins of the Qur'ān, the curious case of the so-called Constitution of Medinah, and what went on during the earliest decades of the Arab conquests. Fred Donner is our guide into unknown territory.

results.trackName: Matthew Melvin-Koushki on Islam, ‘the West’, and Western Esotericism
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We welcome Matthew Melvin-Koushki back to the show to discuss how we might improve our historical picture of western esotericism by including the vast majority of the surviving historical dossier of western esotericism. There's only one problem: in order to do this, we need to embrace the Islamicate world as a major part of the west.

results.trackName: Introducing Islām
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: With Episode 200 the SHWEP has reached a milestone of sorts. We are in the seventh century, and the world-order suddenly changes irrevocably as a new political force arises from Arabia: the Believers. We discuss three main respects in which the history of Islam is the history of western esotericism.

results.trackName: Paul Pasquesi on the Book of the Holy Hierotheos
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss one of the lesser-known, but most esoterically-important, classics of Syriac spiritual literature, the Book of the Holy Hierotheos. Hierotheos was said to have been the teacher of Dionysius the Areopagite, but he wrote in Syriac, and taught a suspiciously-Evagrian practice of ascent to god.

results.trackName: The Pseudo-Dionysios, the Esoteric, and (Christian) Mysticism
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We turn to the questions: What is ‘mystical’ in the Corpus Dionysiacum? What is esoteric? The answers we come up with involve pretty much every aspect of the western esoteric traditions, and, after all the initiatory liturgy, esoteric scriptural hermeneutics, and theandric activity are cleared away, there remains the ascent to ‘the ray of the divine shadow’.

results.trackName: Naming Divine Nothingness: Introducing the Pseudo-Dionysios
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: Into the divine darkness of a hyper-non-existent god walks the Pseudo-Dionysios. In this episode we join many esoteric currents from the antique and late-antique past into a new synthesis which will forever shape western esotericism going forward.

results.trackName: One Empire, Many Names: Reading “Byzantium” with Anthony Kaldellis
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We are delighted to speak with Anthony Kaldellis about ‘Byzantium’, fabled empire full of Greek-speaking Romans which never fell until the fifteenth century, and which plays an outsize role in the history of western esotericism. Come for the historiographical debates about the term ‘Byzantine’, stay for the ‘Byzantine’ court astrology.

results.trackName: Contested Esotericisms at the End of Antiquity: Simplicius, Philoponus, and Olympiodorus
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss three of the most important thinkers from the final generations of philosophical teaching at Alexandria. One is an upstart Christian. Two are esoteric Platonists of the Golden Chain.  One may or may not have been an alchemist.

results.trackName: The Last Platonists? Philosophic Teaching, Christianity, and Polytheism in Late-Antique Alexandria
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss how Platonist philosophical teaching played out at Alexandria before Justinian's edict of 529 and in its aftermath. Featuring cameo appearances from the fall of the western Roman empire and Horapollo's Hieroglyphika.

results.trackName: All from Nothing: Sara Rappe on Damascius
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss the great Damascius, final scholarch of the Athenian Academy, with Sara Rappe. Things become very apophatic.

results.trackName: Hagia Sophia and the Problem of ‘Esoteric Architecture’
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss Justinian's great church, Hagia Sophia, the gem of Constantinople and of Orthodox Christianity. We then look at a number of theories out there which read Hagia Sophia as encoding esoteric messages beneath her Orthodox exterior, and use this case-study as a springboard for discussing the thorny problems involved in interpreting architecture, especially esoteric architecture.

results.trackName: Kevin van Bladel on the Ṣābians of Ḥarrān and the Fate of the Athenian Academy
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss the fascinating town of Ḥarrān (in present-day Türkiye), a place known from late antiquity until at least the eleventh century for its continued tradition of astral, polytheist worship. Kevin van Bladel tells us much to enthral us about this place, but also crushes the dream of a continued tradition of Athenian Late Platonism at Ḥarrān.

results.trackName: Edward Watts on the Age of Justinian and the Closing of the Athenian Academy
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss the life, times, and reign of Justinian, ‘probably the most consequential Roman emperor, at least since Constantine, and maybe since Augustus.’ He transformed the empire; nothing would be the same after his reign. Said reign also saw the closure of the Athenian academy and a number of crucial crises within Christianity, all of which are essential for the history of western esotericism.

results.trackName: Danielle Layne on Proclus’ Religious Life and Thought
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We are delighted to discuss what you might call Proclean spirituality with Danielle Layne. Platonic prayer as a way of living, the erotic quest for the Good, and the ever-elusive Platonic Dyad feature in a wide-ranging conversation combining proper philosophical-historical rigour with the true love of wisdom.

results.trackName: Graeme Miles on Proclus the Commentator
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss Proclus' titanic labours in the field of commentary – on many Platonic dialogues, but also on the Chaldæan Oracles, the Homeric poems, and a number of other texts – with Graeme Miles, an acute reader of Platonist philosophy and part of the team translating Proclus' Republic commentary into English. Come for Platonic commentary as spiritual practice, stay for the kosmic-astrological reading of the Myth of Er.

results.trackName: The Esoteric Proclus, Part II: Esoteric Exegesis and the Occult Ontology of Language
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We enter the interconnected webwork of a reality where signs are things, things are signs, and everything means everything, but appropriately. Come for the visionary semiotics, stay for the occult sigils.

results.trackName: The Esoteric Proclus, Part I: The Life and Thought of an Esoteric Sage
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We look further into Proclus' esoteric doings, as a sage whose privileged status is marked by inspirations and epiphanies, omens and miracles. We then attempt a (shamefully oversimplified) summary of some important aspects of his (meta)physics.

results.trackName: Dylan Burns on Proclus the Successor
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We welcome Dylan Burns back to the podcast to discuss the life, works, and philosophy of Proclus the Successor. ‘All in all, but appropriately to each’

results.trackName: Hierocles of Alexandria and the Pythagorean Golden Verses
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss Hierocles of Alexandria, student of Plutarch of Athens made good. He wrote an esoteric commentary on the poem known as the Golden Verses of the Pythagoreans. The poem is full of good advice and the Commentary tells us a lot about the nature and purification of the luminous subtle body.

results.trackName: The Great God Pan Lives: Introducing the Athenian Academy
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We turn to the final flowering of polytheist Platonist philosophy, centred on Athens (and Alexandria). We review some useful historical data, discuss the history of ‘the Academy’ as a notional ‘school’ in antiquity, and introduce Plutarch of Athens and Syrianus, teachers of the great Proclus.

results.trackName: Ↄ. Martiana on Martianus Capella and the Marriage of Philology and Mercury
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss Martianus Capella and his extraordinary and vexing philological ascent-account, the Marriage of Philology and Mercury. Ↄ. Martiana guides us through a geocentric kosmos where liberal arts are planetary spheres, gods are physical elements, the planets are daimones, but absolutely nothing is as it seems.

results.trackName: Macrobius and the Commentary on Scipio’s Dream
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We explore the rich seam of late-antique esoteric lore that is Macrobius' Commentary on the Dream of Scipio. We discuss who Macrobius was, what he wrote, what he wrote about, and introduce who read him later on. He emerges as a crucial transmitter of astrologised, arithmologically-informed Platonism to the Latin west in the middle ages.

results.trackName: Augustine of Hippo: Saint of the Exoteric
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss Augustine the anti-esotericist, who denies that Christianity has any esoteric dimensions. He employs the esoteric to do so. Can you trust a guy who does that?

results.trackName: The Manichæan Catholic: Augustine of Hippo
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We turn to one of the most difficult, fascinating, and ultimately consequential thinkers of late antiquity, Augustine of Hippo. In this episode we discuss his relationship with Manichæism and Platonist philosophy, and a few of his important philosophical conclusions.

results.trackName: Stephen A. Cooper on Marius Victorinus and Latinate Christian Platonism
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss Marius Victorinus, a fascinating character from the tumultuous Roman scene in the mid fourth century who converted from Platonism to Platonism-plus-Christianity. His life and thought give us a valuable window onto the cultural scene in fourth-century Rome, as well, as some crucial data for the transmission of Platonist ideas into the Latinate middle ages.

results.trackName: Gretchen Reydams-Schils on Calcidius and the Timæus
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss the Latin translation and commentary of Calcidius with Gretchen Reydams-Schils. Who was Calcidius, where did he get his interpretations of what Plato meant, and, best of all, how did his anti-esotericist approach to Plato feed into western Christian esotericisms? We find out.

results.trackName: Plato Latinus
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: The podcast turns from the eastern Roman empire to its western reaches, now falling into strife and decline as we move into the fifth century. In this episode we look at languages, especially Latin and Greek, and discuss how their intelligibility declined in the respective halves of the now-sundered empire. And we discuss the fate of Plato and Platonism in western Europe as we move into a series of episodes discussing late-antique esotericism in Latin.

results.trackName: Jay Bregman on Synesius of Cyrene
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We dive into the fascinating life and thought of Synesius of Cyrene, Platonist philosopher and student of Hypatia of Alexandria, and Orthodox bishop of Ptolemaïs. Committed Christian or pagan bishop? We'll see ....

results.trackName: Noble Lies and Philosophic Silence: Hypatia, Synesius, and the New Esotericism in the Fourth Century
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: Fear, loathing, violence, and persecution. How does the philosopher operate under such circumstances? We look at the case-studies of Hypatia of Alexandria and her student Synesius of Cyrene, for some pointers.

results.trackName: Hypatia of Alexandria: The Life and Death of a Philosopher and her City
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: In Part I of a two-part-series centred around the great Hypatia of Alexandria, we introduce the life, and the notorious death, of the Late Platonist philosopher Hypatia, one of late antiquity's most evocative enigmas. Plus, a Christian mob didn't destroy the Great Library at Alexandria, but that doesn't mean there weren't some scabrous goings-on.

results.trackName: ‘And When Rome Falls, Falls the World’: The Fall of Rome and Western Esotericism
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: The sacking of Rome by Alaric and his Visigoths in the year 410 was an ideologically-charged event that left a permanent imprint on the culture of the west. We discuss two contemporary readings of what this event meant – one a polytheist and one a Christian – and, starting from these case-studies, a few of the crucial themes set in motion by the ‘Fall of Rome’ in the history of western esotericism.

results.trackName: ‘Visibly a Goddess’: Heidi Marx on Sosipatra of Pergamum
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss Sosipatra of Pergamum, an otherwise-unknown late polytheist holy woman and philosopher, depicted by her biographer Eunapius as a living goddess as well as a philosophic teacher in the lineage of Iamblichus. Come for the Late Platonist resistance to Christianity in the fourth century, stay for the mysterious Chaldæan strangers.

results.trackName: Frederico Fidler on Sallustius’ On the Gods and the World
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We are delighted to speak with Frederico Fidler about Sallustius' On the Gods and the World, a short manual of a popular nature outlining how Platonist metaphysics work, how traditional Hellenistic religion is thought to mirror those metaphysical realities, and how esoteric hermeneutics are the key to unlocking the truth in the vast tradition of myth, ritual, and philosophy claimed by Julian, Sallustius, and other late-antique Hellenes. Come for the esoteric myths, stay for the kosmos as esoteric myth.

results.trackName: Strategies of the Esoteric in the Hellenism of the Emperor Julian: Exclusion and Pluralism in a Late-Antique Polytheism
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss the dynamics of Julian's esoteric religious/political formulation of Hellenism, and reflect on some of the very strange things that happen when esoteric religions like Iamblichean theurgy (and Christianity) are taken out of the small conclave and projected onto the corridors of power.

results.trackName: Jeremy Swist on Julian, Part II: The Emperor’s Religio-Philosophic Project
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: Our discussion with Jeremy Swist on The Emperor turns metaphysical, theurgic, and religious, as we discuss Julian's incredible synthesis of Iamblichean theology and metaphysics, traditional religions, and politics. Come for the pagan counter-church, stay for the transcendent solar metaphysics.

results.trackName: Jeremy Swist on the Emperor Julian, Part I: the Political Background and Political Project of the Emperor
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: Jeremy Swist, specialist on Late Platonism, late antiquity, and the great Julian the Faithful, lays out the political background and political project of The Emperor. Part I of a two-part discussion of late antiquity's greatest statesman. No bias here.

results.trackName: Joel Kalvesmaki on Evagrius’ Kephalaia Gnōstika: Philosophy, Scripture, and Apophatic Mysticism
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: In Part II of our discussion with Joel Kalvesmaki we explore the philosophy and mysticism of the Kephalaia Gnōstika, Evagrius' masterwork of mind-bending metaphysical aphorisms.

results.trackName: Joel Kalvesmaki on Evagrius of Pontus, the ‘Gnostic Trilogy’, and the Origenist Controversy
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: Part I of a discussion of Evagrius of Pontus – ascetic, philosopher, developer of Origen's thought, and mystical writer – with Joel Kalvesmaki. In this episode we cover the life and work of the great sage, in particular his ‘gnostic trilogy’, and discuss the ‘Second Origenist Controversy’ which would decide the fate of his opinions vis à vis Orthodoxy in the sixth century.

results.trackName: Theology, Politics, and Radiant Darkness: Michæl Motia on Gregory of Nyssa
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: Having introduced the Cappadocians, we must of course explore the thought of the Divine Gregory of Nyssa. Michæl Motia is our expert guide through the territories both of late-antique religious politics and the illuminated darkness of divine unknowing at the heart of Christian mysticism.

results.trackName: Father Sergey Trostyanskiy on the Cappadocian Fathers, Part II
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: In Part II with Father Sergey, we explore the Platonist ‘mystical’ themes, esoteric imagery of divine darkness, and the limits of human knowledge in the Cappadocians. Христос воскрес!

results.trackName: Father Sergey Trostyanskiy on the Cappadocian Fathers, Part I
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss the great theologians, ascetics, and philosophers of fourth-century Christianity, the Cappadocian Fathers with Father Sergey Trostyanskiy. Come for the Philokalia, the collection which smuggles Origenistic and other anathematised ideas into the very bosom of orthodoxy, stay for the presence of divine darkness to the soul.

results.trackName: Claire Hall on Firmicus Maternus
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: Firmicus Maternus, a fairly prominent fourth-century intellectual from Sicily,  wrote two works which survive: one is our earliest-surviving manual of astrological practice in Latin, and it shows a full-blooded belief in astral determinism, and the second is a rabid Christian polemic against traditional religious practices. Discuss.

results.trackName: Kocku von Stuckrad on Monotheist Astrologies in (Late) Antiquity
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: ‘With the rise of monotheism in the late Roman world, astrology became a forbidden science and began its long decline.’ Starting from this widespread, and completely false historical myth, we discuss the realities of monotheist astrologies across antiquity and beyond with Professor Kocku von Stuckrad.

results.trackName: Metals, Temples, and Living Statues: Shannon Grimes on Zosimus’ Egyptian Context
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We fill in some of the historical, cultural, and economic background of Zosimus' life and practice with Shannon Grimes. Come for the economics of metallurgy and ancient Egyptian trade-guilds, stay for the living statues.

results.trackName: Bink Hallum on the Extended Zosimus
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We further explore the thought of Zosimus of Panopolis with Dr Bink Hallum, whose PhD research centred on the Arabic Zosimean corpus. We cover the basic (if confusing) textual situation, and then discuss astral influences, daimones and demons, mysterious talismans, Enochic ideas, and much more.

results.trackName: Matteo Martelli Introduces Zosimus of Panopolis
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss the life, work, and thought of Zosimus of Panopolis, greatest alchemist of late antiquity, with Professor Matteo Martelli. All is One!

results.trackName: Recognising the Real in the Forgery: The Pseudo-Clementine Literature
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss the extraordinary late-antique novel of the early Christian church at Rome, known as the Pseudo-Clementine literature. Gnosticism, Jewish-Christianity, esotericism, scriptural and other forgery, and the problem of authenticity itself loom large as we quite improperly discuss a text meant only for true initiates.

results.trackName: Charles Häberl on the Mandæans
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: In one of the single most fascinating interviews we have ever had the pleasure of conducting, we speak with Charles Häberl on the Mandæans, a living religious tradition of Mesopotamia, now largely living in a global diaspora, which is the single Gnostic religion surviving from late antiquity. Forget Nag-Hammadi; it's all about San Antonio.

results.trackName: Paul Pasquesi on Christian Asceticism in the Late-Antique Syriac World
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We explore the fascinating world of early Christian asceticism in the Syriac-speaking world of late antiquity. Paul Pasquesi is our guide to everything from the basic historical context to the extreme forms of practice engaged in by these eastern Christians in search of divine revelations.

results.trackName: Korshi Dosoo on Early Christian Magic
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: With papyrologist Korshi Dosoo as our guide, we explore the world of first-millennium Christian magic as it is found in the papyrus-records, both published and unpublished. Along the way we learn more about Christianity than we expected.

results.trackName: Prolegomena to Christian Magic
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We set the stage for an examination of early Christian magical traditions, starting from the authoritative writings of the church fathers, who deny that there is such a thing as Christian magic, and insist that polytheist religion is the real sorcery. Then it turns out that there is lots and lots of Christian magic from late antiquity.

results.trackName: The Testament of Solomon and the Solomonic Tradition, Part II
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We explore the astral-demonic lore, the angelic medicine, and the many legendary stories recorded in the Testament of Solomon, and some of the manifold traditions which flow out from this legendary corpus. Come for the Testament, stay for the Pentagram!

results.trackName: The Testament of Solomon and the Solomonic Tradition, Part I
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We want to discuss the Testament of Solomon, an extraordinary demonological, angelogical, astrological, magical work from late antiquity. But we realise that, to get there, we need to spend some time exploring the earlier reaches of the ‘Solomonic tradition’. So we do. Come for the building of the First Temple, stay for the cloud upon the sanctuary.

results.trackName: Exploring the Sefer ha-Razim
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We explore the earliest-known Jewish ‘magic book’, the Sefer ha-Razim or Book of Mysteries. Angel-magic meets addressative practices aimed at old friends like Helios and Hermes, while Hellenistic astral cosmology collides with fiery heavenly palace-firmaments of the apocalyptic and Hekhalotic stamp.

results.trackName: Curses! Sarah Veale on Roman ‘Curse-Tablets’
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We turn from the far-eastern, Jewish magic of the incantation-bowls to the far-western, polytheist magic of the Roman ‘curse-tablets’. Expect intriguing similarities across cultural divides, along with important differences. Featuring the Great Mother goddess, Isis, and a number of supporting players.

results.trackName: Daniel James Waller on the Jewish Incantation-Bowls
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We dive more deeply into the enigmatic corpus of late-antique Jewish ‘incantation bowls’ from Mesopotamia with the help of researcher Daniel Waller. We discuss the bowls as material objects, functional technology, and their place in late-antique Jewish culture.

results.trackName: Gideon Bohak on Late-Antique Jewish Magic
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: Gideon Bohak provides us with a superb introduction to the evidence for late-antique Jewish magic and to what that evidence tells us. Introducing the essential book of Jewish magic, the Sefer ha-Razim.

results.trackName: Thinking through Monotheism, Henotheism, Polytheism, and Dualism in Late Antiquity
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We wander through a bunch of important (but mushy) ideas helpful for understanding late antiquity and late-antique religion: monotheism, henotheism, polytheism, and dualism. Featuring the triumphant return of Rupert and Steve, and they brought some friends.

results.trackName: Politics and Religion in Late Antiquity, Part II: The Rise of Christianity and the Invention and Eclipse of ‘Paganism’
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We dive into the history of late-antique Rome from the perspective of Jews, Christians, ‘pagans’, ‘heretics’, and others vis à vis the Roman state, and give some partial explanations for how the ‘impossible’ happened, and the Empire became the Christian Empire.

results.trackName: Politics and Religion in Late Antiquity, Part I: Geopolitics, Empire, and Rabbinic Judaism
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: At the end of the the third century, the podcast dives back into the realm where politics meets religion. In Part I, we discuss the geopolitical balance of the Roman and Sassanian states, the position of the Jews in late antiquity, and the basics of the future of Jewry, a new form of Jewish life and religion known as Rabbinic Judaism.

results.trackName: Run the Numbers: The Theology of Arithmetic
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We explore the Theolegoumena arithmeticæ, the ‘Theology of Arithmetic’, our most complete extant arithmological treatise from antiquity. It tells us a lot about Neopythagorean theory of number in the Greek ‘alphanumeric age’, it may be by Iamblichus, and it informs us that the Dyad is ‘Daring’.

results.trackName: Brian Alt on Sacred Materials, Divine Names, and Subtle Physiology in Iamblichean Theurgy
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We explore the nitty-gritty of the ritual acts lying behind the theoretical discussions in the De mysteriis. Brian Alt is our guide on a journey through Iamblichean theurgy, its many parallels in Hermetica and ‘magical’ papyri from Egypt, and its echoes in earlier and later Platonism.

results.trackName: Gregory Shaw on the Phenomenology of Iamblichean Theurgy
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss the phenomenology and meaning of theurgy with Professor Gregory Shaw, whose many publications on the Sage of Chalcis have helped to free his religious ideas from the opprobrium of a century of scholarship and reposition them where they belong: as spiritual practices of late-antique philosophy.

results.trackName: John Finamore on Iamblichean Theurgy in Theory and Practice
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss the practices lying behind the descriptions in the De mysteriis, and the theory behind the practices. Professor John Finamore is our guide through the labyrinth of evidence about theurgy.

results.trackName: The Great Theurgy Debate: Porphyry’s Letter to Anebo, Iamblichus’ Response, and the Question(s) of Ritual
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: In a digression-filled survey, we attempt to give some idea of Porphyry's Letter to Anebo, of Iamblichus' responses to that Letter, and the general theological/practical approach found in the De mysteriis, antiquity's greatest philosophic manifesto for addressative ritual practice.

results.trackName: The Esoteric Iamblichus
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss the rich strata of the esoteric in the work of the sage of Chalcis. Starting from the evidence for socially-esoteric teaching within Iamblichus' school, we move on to discuss his constructions of esoteric wisdom lineages – notably the tradition of ‘the theurgists’ – his employment of tropes of hiding and revealing, and the parameters of the Iamblichean ‘ineffable’.

results.trackName: The ‘Greater Kinds’, Souls, and Kosmos: Iamblichus’ Philosophy, Part II
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We enter into the kosmic reaches of Iamblichus' universe, populated by a host of fascinating fauna, including archangels, angels, daimones, heroes, archontes, and even – weirdest of all – human beings.

results.trackName: Esoteric Hermeneutics, Divine Hierarchy, and the Ineffable: The Philosophy of Iamblichus, Part I
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We explore Iamblichus' extraordinary ‘esoteric-literalist’ approach to the Platonic corpus and the upper reaches of his complex metaphysics, the realms of the One(s) and the noetic-noeric levels of reality. Featuring special guest-star the Noeric Hebdomad.

results.trackName: Introducing Iamblichus of Chalcis
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We introduce Iamblichus, known to later Platonists as ‘the Divine’, ‘the Great Iamblichus’, Platonist philosopher and wonder-working holy-man. Come for the basic biographical summary and discussion of the Iamblichean corpus of writings, stay for the levitation and miraculous apparitions.

results.trackName: A Word to Conjure With: On ‘Theurgy’ in Late Antiquity and Beyond
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We talk about theurgy: what, where, when, and, indeed, how? It's more complicated than we thought. Come for the Chaldæan Oracles, stay for the Technical Brutal Death Metal.

results.trackName: Astral Accretions, Fate, and the Resurrection-Body: Other Subtle Bodies of Antiquity
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss other subtle-body theories in antique esoteric literature from the Hermetica, the Platonists, Basilides, Origen, and other esoteric Christians, looking at theories of astral accretions, counterfeit spirits, resurrection-bodies, and more.

results.trackName: Soul-Flight, Noetic Bodies, and Pneumatic Vehicles: Toward a History of the Platonist Subtle Body
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss the soul-flight practices found in our testimonies to the ancient Greek iatromanteis, Middle-Platonist and other early testimony to the theory of a soul-vehicle, and the subtle-body theories of Plotinus and Porphyry.

results.trackName: Methodologies for Studying the Subtle Body
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We formally introduce the ‘subtle body’, the mysterious tertium quid which, alongside the soul and the physical body, occupies a central place in the anthropologies of many esoteric traditions. Featuring the triumphant return of Doctor Strange to the podcast.

results.trackName: Nilüfer Akçay on Porphyry’s On the Cave of the Nymphs
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We speak with Nilüfer Akçay, author of the only full-length English monograph on Porphyry's On the Cave of the Nymphs.

results.trackName: Porphyry and the Barbarians: Ethnicity, Religious Practice, and Esoteric Interpretation
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We get into Porphyry's reception of Greek and non-Greek wisdom, and the ways in which esoteric truth is to be found in various cultural locales. We also discuss the one place where it is most definitely not to be found: Christianity.

results.trackName: Dorian Greenbaum on Porphyry and Astrology
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We talk astrology in Porphyry with Dorian Greenbaum, historian of astrology and philosophy. Along the way we situate ourselves within the history of astrology in the third century, discuss astrological world-views, and consider whether the oikodespotēs is the same chap as the personal daimōn.

results.trackName: Porphyry’s Gods: The Metaphysics and Physics of Divinity
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss the universe of Porphyry, which is crawling with gods, powers, and daimones, and some of the ways a human being might expect to navigate such a place. The episode features a long discursus on the theory of metempsychosis and a brief discursus on divine possession.

results.trackName: ‘Poet, Philosopher, Hierophant’: Introducing Porphyry of Tyre
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We introduce Porphyry of Tyre, a most prolific Platonist writer and thinker. Come for the Platonist metaphysics, stay for the esoteric reading-strategies, exorcisms, divine possessions, and lost work on the River Styx.

results.trackName: Charles M. Stang on the Divine Double in Late Antiquity
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss the motif of the divine twin, angelic counterpart, personal daimōn, and other forms of higher, divine self with Charles Stang. We may not be who we think we are, but that's good news.

results.trackName: Jason BeDuhn on Mani and Manichæism
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss one of the most anomalous, vexing, and fascinating religious movements in history, the first to span east and west, the elusive but crucial Manichæism, and its prophet, the great Apostle of Light, Mani. The eternal struggle between light and darkness is on, and minds will be blown.

results.trackName: Radcliffe G. Edmonds III on the ‘Mithrasliturgie’
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss PGM IV 475-824, the famous ‘Mithrasliturgie’, with Radcliffe G. Edmonds III. Come for the immortalisation, divinisation, and visionary cosmic ascent, stay for the magical crocodile-surfing.

results.trackName: Mithras and the Stars: Astral Elements in the Cult of Mithras
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss all the amazing astral imagery associated with Mithraic temples, the extraordinary testimonies to ascent of the Mithraic soul given by Celsus and Porphyry, and ask what it all means. Salvation, astral ascent, initiatory mysteries, and weird planetary orderings abound.

results.trackName: Mysteries of the Rock-Born God: The Roman Cult of Mithras
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We introduce the enigmatic evidence for an innovative initiatory cult of the Roman empire, the mysteries of Mithras. Come for the underground cave-temples, stay for the mysterious ravens and uncomfortably-placed scorpions.

results.trackName: Jean-Marc Narbonne on Plotinus in Dialogue with the Gnostics
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: A leading scholar of the interconnections between Plotinus' thought and the thought of the Gnostics whom he disliked so much, Jean-Marc Narbonne discusses some of the Plotinian texts and ideas which make more sense if we see them in dialogue with the Gnostics.

results.trackName: Dylan Burns on Sethian Gnosticism
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss the Platonistic Sethian tractates and the movements which lay behind them with Copticist and scholar of Platonistic esotericism Dylan Burns. Ancient texts, methodological distinctions, cosmic catastrophe, and salvation abound.

results.trackName: The Esoteric Plotinus, Part II: Unsaying the Real
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss the ineffable in Plotinus: how it is deployed, how it is esoteric, how scholars have tried to deal with it, and how not least among its paradoxical functions is to call us to the highest initiation.

results.trackName: Plotinus on Astrology with Marilynn Lawrence
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We speak with Marilynn Lawrence, authority on Platonism, Hellenistic astrology, and the intersection of the two, about Plotinus' theoretical writings on the science of the stars.

results.trackName: The Esoteric Plotinus, Part I: Philosophic Silence and Esoteric Reading
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss aspects of the esoteric found in two distinct sources – Porphyry's Life of Plotinus and Plotinus' own writings – and think through them. The esoteric Platonist exegete meets the late pagan holy man; are they the same person?

results.trackName: Plotinus the Magician? Ritual Practice and Power in Platonism
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss Plotinus on ‘magic’, in theory, and, yes, in practice. Come for magic as applied physics, stay for the apotropaic chickens.

results.trackName: Mateusz Stróżyński on Spiritual Practices in Plotinus
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss Plotinian anthropology and spiritual practices with Mateusz Stróżyński. Come for the stripping away of the illusory, bodily self, stay for the luminous, all-encompassing sphere of the higher reality.

results.trackName: We are the One: Plotinus’ Participatory Metaphysics
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: Plotinus' universe is uniquely full of the human self, which extends all the way from the sucking mud of matter's non-existence to the ultimate profundity of the One's non-existence, and all the existent bits in-between. We discuss some of the ways in which this human metaphysical terrain is explored in the Enneads.

results.trackName: ‘The Philosopher of our Time’: Introducing Plotinus
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: Plotinus was the greatest philosopher of late antiquity, and one of the most crucial thinkers for the long story of western esotericism. We introduce his amazing philosophy and the basics of his biography.

results.trackName: Matthew Neujahr on the Sibylline Oracles
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss the Sibylline Oracles, a strange, sprawling, extremely complex collection of oracular hexameters from antiquity. Matthew Neujahr is our guide through a textual and prophetic labyrinth of ancient woman sages, Hellenic, Jewish, and Christian prophetic concerns, and the high uncanny.

results.trackName: Christian Bull on the Way of Hermes in Antiquity
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: In our final episode in the Hermetica series, we discuss the way of Hermes in antiquity with Christian Hervik Bull. Come for the renunciation, immortalisation, and hypercosmic ascent, stay for the animated statues.

results.trackName: Anna van den Kerchove on the Hermetic Way in Antiquity
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We speak with Anna van den Kerchove, a leading voice in the scholarly trend ‘reclaiming’ ancient Hermetism from its long sojourn outside the realms of respectability. We discuss Hermetic texts and the kinds of milieux in which they may have circulated in antiquity.

results.trackName: M. David Litwa on Deification in the Hermetica
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss the important Hermetic idea (or should that be ‘practice’?) of becoming divine with Dr M. David Litwa, who has devoted considerable thought to the matter of deification. A fascinating conversation emerges, and Litwa blows our mind.

results.trackName: Silent Encounters: The Esoteric in the Ancient Hermetica
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We concentrate on the elements of the esoteric in the Hermetica that we have covered in the last few episodes, and discuss C.H. XIII and The Ogdoad Reveals the Ennead, our two most esoteric Hermetica.

results.trackName: Other Hermetic Worlds: The Asclepius and Korê Kosmou
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss two world-building Hermetic texts from antiquity, the Latin Asclepius and the Korê Kosmou. We have seen Hermes as visionary pupil of the divine consciousness; now we see him as ancient esoteric sage, prophet of doom, and cosmic planetary deity.

results.trackName: Wouter Hanegraaff on the Poimandres
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: Wouter Hanegraaff has been reading the Poimandres with great attention. Come for the visionary encounter with the divine nous, stay for cosmogenesis-as-love-story.

results.trackName: Corpus Hermeticum I, the Poimandres
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss the Poimandres, perhaps the most extraordinary Hermetic document surviving from antiquity. It's an apocalyptic vision granting gnôsis of how the world was created, how humanity came to be the way we are, and what we can do about it. Essential reading.

results.trackName: Professor Christian Wildberg on Emending the Corpus Hermeticum
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss the (poor) state of the texts collected in the Corpus Hermeticum with Professor Christian Wildberg, a man who proposes to do something about it.

results.trackName: Brian Copenhaver on the Hermetica
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We speak with Brian Copenhaver, translator of the Corpus Hermeticum and general man of parts vis á vis all things hermetic, to get some orientation on the ancient Hermetica and what they are all about.

results.trackName: Thrice-Greatest Hermes
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We introduce the sage of sages, the barbarian philosopher of philosophers, the one and only (unless there were more of him) Thrice-Greatest Hermes. We also introduce his copious literary output, the Hermetica, and discuss these writings in an introductory way.

results.trackName: Total War: Polemical Esotericism in the Contra Celsum
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We explore the polemics and counter-polemics of Origen's Contra Celsum, with a particular eye toward the use (and abuse) of the esoteric as a strategy of tradition-building, exclusion, and totalising interpretation.

results.trackName: The True Account: Celsus, Origen, and Ideological Esotericism in Late Antiquity
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: An almost-unknown Middle Platonist philosopher named Celsus wrote the first-known anti-Christian polemical pamphlet some time in the later second century. This is The True Account. It is esoteric.

results.trackName: Aron Reppmann Introduces Origen of Alexandria
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: Professor Aron Reppmann introduces the life, thought, and esotericism of Origen of Alexandria, one of the greatest church-fathers, Platonist theologian par excellence, and revolutionary scriptural exegete.

results.trackName: From Word to Silence: The Rise of the Apophatic in Late Antiquity
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: As antiquity progressed, certain esoteric religious thinkers and philosophers came increasingly to doubt whether the nature of the highest reality could be expressed in words. They developed a new form of language to deal with the problem of talking about the ineffable: apophasis. We discuss speaking the silence in late antiquity.

results.trackName: The Third Century and (the Long) Late Antiquity
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: As the podcast enters the third century, we discuss the parameters of ‘late antiquity’, and what makes something ‘late-antique’. Special bonus material: the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire!

results.trackName: Becoming Gods: Divinisation and Angelomorphic Transformation in Clement
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss Clement's endgame, where the Gnostic encounters god face-to-face after a lengthy transformative evolution into higher and higher spiritual forms. Things get seriously esoteric.

results.trackName: Henny Fiskå Hägg on Clement’s Apophatic Writing
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We speak with Professor Henny Fiskå Hägg about the apophatic theory and writing-practice of Clement of Alexandria, one of antiquity's finest exponents of the art of writing about that-about-which-nothing-can-be-written.

results.trackName: Lifting the Veil: Esoteric Reading in Clement’s Stromateis
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: Clement stays esoteric. We examine the esoteric wisdom-lineages constructed by Clement, how he reads them, in the context of how he hides his reading of them. Plus, there seems to have been some genuine, contemporary esotericism going on in early Christianity.

results.trackName: Mystagogic Patchwork: Esoteric Writing in Clement’s Stromateis
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We explore the esoteric writing methodologies of Clement's Stromateis – the innovative ‘public secrecy’, the reasons for Clement's esotericism, and the evocation of the mysteries and of the ineffable as aspects of esoteric rhetoric.

results.trackName: The Orthodox Gnostic: Introducing Clement of Alexandria
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We introduce the life and thought of Orthodox Christianity's favourite in-house Gnostic, the great Clement of Alexandria. Come for the philosophical, esoteric Christianity, stay for the  progressive postmortem deification.

results.trackName: The Astrology of Vettius Valens
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We examine the life, work, and legacy of Vettius Valens, second-century Roman astrologer and author of the  Anthologies, the most hard-core practical handbook of astrological practice which survives from antiquity.

results.trackName: Claudius Ptolemy and the Tetrabiblos
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss Claudius Ptolemy (no relation), synthesiser of Hellenistic astronomy/astrology to the mediæval world and beyond, and his two great works, the Almagest and the Tetrabiblos. Come for the naturalistic account of astral causation, stay for the planetary talismans.

results.trackName: Numerical Mysteries: Nichomachus of Gerasa, Arithmology, and Second-Century Neopythagoreanism
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: Speculations about the properties of number have been a major constituent of some western esoteric traditions. In this episode we examine the most important source of much of this tradition of arithmological thought, first- and second-century Neopythagoreanism, and the writings of one crucial thinker in particular: Nicomachus of Gerasa.

results.trackName: Matteo Martelli on the Pseudo-Democritus
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: In the previous episode we surveyed alchemy from its beginnings to the present day; in this episode we go back to the roots. Matteo Martelli has produced the first critical edition of the fragments of the Pseudo-Democritus, our earliest-known work of alchemy. We discuss the secrets found within its pages.

results.trackName: Introducing Alchemy with Lawrence Principe
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: Here it finally is: Alchemy! This interview is a superb introduction to the Hermetick Art from Lawrence Principe, a man who knows how to ‘read, read, read’, but also how to practice.

results.trackName: Other Gospels and Alien Gods: Marcion of Sinope
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We look at Marcion of Sinope, the final arch-heretic in our ‘unholy trinity’. Marcion compiled the first Christian textual canon – he wrote the first Bible – but this was not your grandma's Bible. Demiurgy, transcendence, and some interesting questions of textual hermeneutics abound.

results.trackName: Geoffrey Smith on Valentinus and Valentinianism
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: Under the expert guidance of Geoffrey Smith, we explore the world-view of Valentinus – an elite intellectual Christian thinker of the second century – and his legacy – a reputation for the blackest heresy and a demiurgical Christian movement known nowadays as Valentinianism.

results.trackName: I Got Soul, And I’m Super Bad: Basilides of Alexandria
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: Basilides of Alexandria, one of the first Christian philosophers and scriptural exegetes, is known as one of the great Gnostic heresiarchs of the second century. But what did he actually teach? It's mind-blowing and it's esoteric.

results.trackName: Warfaring Strangers: Prolegomena to Second-Century Christianity
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We take a deep breath before diving into detailed discussions of early esoteric Christianities to consider a few key terms and their historical development. What was orthodoxy? What was heresy? Who were the heresiologists, and what were they doing?

results.trackName: Michael Williams on the Trouble with ‘Gnosticism’
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: Professor Michael Williams leads us on a tour of ‘Gnosticism’, both as a term (used and misused by ancient heresiologists, Reformation-era polemicists, modern scholars, and even modern ‘Gnostics’) and as a group of late-ancient religious texts which are very, very interesting, but which should probably not be called ‘Gnostic’.

results.trackName: Alone with the Alone: Numenius’ Metaphysics
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We explore the philosophy of Numenius, in which we see the stirrings of a new type of apophatic discourse of transcendence which will come to be definitive of late antique metaphysics and theology.

results.trackName: Inter philosophos occultorum curiosior: Numenius of Apamea
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We investigate the esoteric practice of one of Middle Platonism's most enigmatic figures, the great Numenius of Apamea.

results.trackName: Korshi Dosoo on the Papyri Græcæ Magicæ and Western Esotericism
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We speak with papyrologist Korshi Dosoo about the history, interpretation, and makeup of the body of documents known nowadays as the Greek Magical Papyri. It all starts in ancient Egypt, but it doesn't stop until Aleister Crowley and the Mormons have made an appearance.

results.trackName: The Chaldæan Oracles and Theurgy
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We have looked at what kind of world the Chaldæan Oracles set forth. We turn now to the ways in which the  adept navigates that world – through ritual, epiphanic visions, cognitive disciplines, talismans, and by leaving the body through breathing. This is theurgy, and esoteric religion in antiquity would never be the same again.

results.trackName: The Chaldæan Oracles
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We introduce one of the most extraordinary and influential texts of antiquity for the history of western esotericism: the Chaldæan Oracles. We discuss questions of authorship (Julian the Theurge, the Gods, or the Soul of Plato?) and the mythic metaphysics found in the text.

results.trackName: I’m Not Sorry: The Apology of Apuleius
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: In this episode we discuss the defense-speech of Apuleius against charges of having used magic to make a wealthy widow fall in love with him. Roman law, sorcery, and philosophy collide in a rhetorical tour-de-force, and we discuss whether fish are magical or not.

results.trackName: Ineffable Initiations and Golden Asses: Apuleius of Madauros and the Metamorphoses
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: Apuleius was a great Latin-language Middle Platonist writer, whose works preserve some fascinating esoteric materials which had a major impact on the development of western esotericism in the Latin middle ages and beyond. We introduce the man and his famous occult novel, the  Metamorphoses, or Golden Ass.

results.trackName: Hypochondria and Epiphany: The Strange Case of Ælius Aristides
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We examine one of the strangest records of personal religious experience and divine epiphany from antiquity, the Hieroi Logoi of Ælius Aristides. Come for the incubation, dream-initiations, and miraculous powers, stay for the interminable descriptions of dyspepsia.

results.trackName: Daniel Harris-McCoy on the Oneirocritica of Artemidorus
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: With an expert guide, we enter the labyrinth of second-century divinatory dream-interpretation. Artemidorus' Oneirocritica is the west's earliest surviving manual of dream-interpretation, and it's amazing.

results.trackName: Gil Renberg on Incubation
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: In antiquity the gods sometimes communicated with mortals through dreams. But sometimes the gods can be fickle; in cases like this, you need to head to the sanctuary and go see the god at home. You need ritualised dreaming, or incubation.

results.trackName: Plutarch’s Myths of Cosmic Ascent
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: In this episode we look at three different homemade myths found in Plutarch's writings. All of them deal with the fate of the soul after death, all of them put the land of the dead in the sky, and all of them are exceedingly difficult to interpret. We have seen Plutarch interpret a myth esoterically; now we see him making his own esoteric myths.

results.trackName: Plutarch’s On Isis and Osiris
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We look at Plutarch's tour de force of esoteric hermeneutics, the On Isis and Osiris. Egyptian myth meets Greek esoteric Platonism, and something new is born.

results.trackName: An Erudite Esotericist: Introducing Plutarch of Chæronea
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We introduce Plutarch of Chæronea: first-century man-of-letters, pioneering biographer, and transmitter of ancient esoteric Platonism to the western tradition.

results.trackName: Astrology, Politics, and Platonism in the Early Empire: The Case of Thrasyllus
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We look at the fascinating figure of Thrasyllus: astrologer, power-player in the imperial Roman court of Tiberius, philosopher … and editor of the works of Plato.

results.trackName: Graeme Miles on Apollonius of Tyana
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: Apollonius of Tyana was a first-century wandering philosopher-sage, famous in later tradition as a great Pythagorean and wonder-working holy man. We look at the man himself and at his powerful myth.

results.trackName: The Enigma of Early Christianity
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We introduce Christianity. Just how did this movement get started in the first place? The crazy thing is, no one knows.

results.trackName: Dylan Burns on the ‘Underworld of Platonism’
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: Building on our previous episode, where we introduced 'Middle Platonism', in this interview we investigate the middle Platonist 'Underworld', religio-philosophical texts of antiquity which became mainstays of later western esoteric traditions:  the Chaldæan Oracles, the Hermetica, and the Gnostic tractates.

results.trackName: John Dillon on Middle Platonism
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: Under the expert guidance of Professor John Dillon, we begin our exploration of what may be antiquity’s single most crucial current for the development of western esotericism: Middle Platonism.

results.trackName: The Esoteric and the State in Ancient Rome, Part 2: The State and the Stars
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We trace the rise of the Hellenistic divinatory art of astrology through the Roman Republic into the first century of the Empire, and investigate how an esoteric science became a matter of highest concern to the Roman state.  Expect uprisings, assassinations, and executions. Astrology used to be really exciting.

results.trackName: The Esoteric and the State in Ancient Rome, Part 1: Late Republican Esotericism
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: In the first of a two-episode series exploring the relationship between state power and esoteric ideas in the late Roman Republic and early empire, we look at what it meant to be esoteric at Rome, and investigate some upper-class Roman esotericists.

results.trackName: Introducing Rome
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: The Eternal City, and the empire she built, cast a long shadow down the ages. This episode consists of some preliminary historical musings on Rome, and, more importantly, on the idea of Rome.

results.trackName: Justin Rogers on Philo in Early Christianity
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: Justin Rogers guides us on a tour of the afterlife of Philo's work. How did the great Hellenistic Jewish thinker become a father of the Christian faith (and of Christian esoteric scriptural hermeneutics in particular)? We find out.

results.trackName: The Esoteric Philo
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: In this episode we explore the deeply esoteric thought of Philo of Alexandria. Expect hidden ancient perennial traditions, divine revelation, esoteric philosophic truths hidden in plain sight, arithmological speculations, and much more.

results.trackName: The First Western Esotericist: Philo of Alexandria
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: The first true western esotericist: Philo of Alexandria. In this episode we come to grips with what makes him so western, what makes him so esoteric, and introduce his fascinating life and work.

results.trackName: Naomi Janowitz on Jewish Magic and ‘The Jewish Magi’ in Antiquity
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: The Jews in antiquity were busy doing rituals of all sorts, many of which scholars want to call magical. They were also seen by their neighbours as especially skilled at various ritual arts which the neighbours called magical. Naomi Janowitz discusses Jewish magic and the ‘Jewish Magi’ in antiquity.

results.trackName: Frances Flannery on Jewish Dreams in Antiquity
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: In an interview bringing together both the visionary narratives of apocalyptic and the practical side of the Hekhalot traditions, Professor Frances Flannery leads us through the corridors of dreaming and the esoteric in antique Judaism.

results.trackName: Palaces of Heavenly Wisdom: The Hekhalot and Merkavah Traditions
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We give an overview of the complex and fascinating Hekhalot and Merkavah texts, works not only describing the journey to God’s throne, but giving instructions on how to get there, and not merely enumerating the angelic hierarchies, but giving the tools to summon and command them.

results.trackName: Enoch, Apocalyptic, and Abrahamic Faith
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: In this episode we explore further the amazing work 1 Enoch, taking in along the way ruminations on the history of the west, debates about the identity of the Enochic authors, and some hints as to the development of the Enochic tradition as a western esoteric ‘scripture’.

results.trackName: Enoch and the Book of Watchers
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: The text known as 1 Enoch is perhaps the greatest work of apocalyptic literature, and a kind of esoteric scripture within Judaism, Christianity, and Gnosticism. We meet the text and look at the evil giants and celestial visions of its first part, the Book of Watchers.

results.trackName: John J. Collins on Apocalyptic
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: In this episode Professor John J. Collins introduces a fascinating product of Second Temple Judaism, and a fertile vehicle for esoteric speculation beyond the bounds of Jewry – apocalyptic literature. All will be revealed!

results.trackName: The Long Secret History of the Jews Part II: Second-Temple Judaism
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: Judaism starts to get seriously esoteric in the time known as the Second Temple period. This episode gives some basic historical points of reference for this era of Jewish antiquity, setting the stage for the visionary journeys, apocalyptic revelations, and magic to come.

results.trackName: Pythagoras Revived: An Anatomy of Neopythagoreanism
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: After the final Pythagorean died, all was quiet. And then, suddenly, people started going around calling themselves Pythagoreans. Growing long beards. Hailing Pythagoras as an ancient magus-sage. Positing a monad as the ultimate source of reality. Welcome to Neopythagoreanism.

results.trackName: The Numbers Don’t Lie: Joel Kalvesmaki on ‘Pythagorean’ Number
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: Whenever anyone does something  other than arithmetic with numbers, the name Pythagoras tends to crop up. Exactly how this strange situation came about is a fascinating story, and Dr Kalvesmaki has done groundbreaking work on the subject. This episode is a superb introduction to the origins of ‘gematria’ and arithmology.

results.trackName: After Pythagoras
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: When we last visited the Pythagoreans, they were going through some difficult times. In this episode we discuss what happened next. Pythagoreanism is dead, long live Pythagoreanism!

results.trackName: Stoic Physics and Esoteric Metaphysics
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: The Stoics had a naturalistic physical theory which, strangely, had a huge influence both on esoteric spirituality and on occult sciences. In this, our final episode on Stoicism, we discuss three key terms from Stoic physics and their surprising afterlives in western esotericism.

results.trackName: Esoteric Hermeneutics in Stoicism
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: The contribution of Stoicism to the art of esoteric reading, both of texts and of the secret correspondences within the universe, is little studied. This episode sifts the evidence to set the record straight.

results.trackName: Christopher Gill on Stoicism
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: Strangely enough, one of the least 'esoteric' schools of antique philosophy, the Stoics, had a profound influence on a number of aspects of western esotericism. In this episode we learn the basics of what they were about from an expert.

results.trackName: Chris Brennan on Hellenistic Astrology
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: Historical discussions often fail to help us 'get inside' the subject we are looking at. In this episode we talk to Chris Brennan, Hellenistic astrologer and historian, for some theoretical and practical light on the realities of ancient astrology.

results.trackName: Fate and Foreknowledge: Toward Hellenistic Astrology
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: The synthesis of Mesopotamian, Egyptian, and Greek sciences of the stars gave rise to the art of astrology in Hellenistic Egypt. Astrology went on to become a defining aspect of western culture, and the master-discipline of western esotericism. We look at how it happened.

results.trackName: Wheels Within Wheels: Toward Western Esoteric Cosmology
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We are moving with astral ineluctability toward the birth of true astrology in the Hellenistic period. But first we need to get from Mesopotamian astronomy to the Greek world. This episode bridges the gap between middle-eastern astral science and the Hellenistic flourishing of Greek astronomy.

results.trackName: The Esoteric Aristotle, Part 2
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: In this episode we survey the philosophical and occult Pseudo-Aristotles of late antiquity and the middle ages, dipping into a couple of wonderful manuscripts along the way.

results.trackName: The Esoteric Aristotle, Part I
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: Aristotle might not spring to mind when contemplating the names of esoteric heroes of the past. But the figure of Plato's greatest student in fact had an esoteric afterlife to rival that of Plato himself!

results.trackName: Peter Adamson on Plato
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: We discuss Plato with Peter Adamson, Professor of Philosophy at the LMU in Munich and presenter of the History of Philosophy Podcast, asking the question: how can the Plato of analytic philosophy be the same man as the esoteric Plato?

results.trackName: Plato’s Parmenides and Metaphysics
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: At the heart of western esotericism lies a space where logic becomes something that transcends logic; Plato's dialogue the Parmenides is perhaps the first work to occupy that space. Join us for a look at Plato's most baffling work.

results.trackName: Mystery and Immortality: Plato’s Phædo
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
results.description: The Phædo depicts Socrates' final hours, spent in philosophical discussion with his circle of friends. Socrates argues that the soul is immortal, and that the philosopher should rejoice to die. But his reasons for believing this are ... mysterious.

results.trackName: Mystery and Initiation in Plato
results.collectionName: Podcast episodes – The Secret History of Western Esotericism Podcast (SHWEP)
